newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia bill interest pushes yield to target lows.
newsitem.headline: Russia bill interest pushes yield to target lows.

text.p: Strong investor interest at Wednesday's auction of 364-day GKO discount Treasury bills allowed the Finance Ministry to push yields to levels forecast for the year-end but dealers said it may be hard to sustain these levels.
"The yield is too low and given the current shortage of roubles it will be difficult to hold it," International Moscow Bank dealer Yevgeny Krayev said.

Interest in the 105-day bills was less than on the one-year paper and banks which had bid above non-competitive bids were paid above the market level, but the yield -- a record low for a T-bill auction -- came in lower than on the 364-day bills because of the shorter maturity.
"The results of the 105-day auction showed us that the Finance Ministry had a guaranteed demand at the second auction, that's why the yield could have been any low," Krayev said.
From the first auction the Finance Ministry received less than half of what was necessary for repayment.
"The yield is too low and given the current shortage of roubles it will be difficult to hold it," Krayev said.
